name: Asynchritus
overview: Asynchritus is a male figure mentioned in the New Testament to whom the Apostle Paul sends greetings. There is no information about his tribal affiliation or other personal details. His mention in Romans 16:14 indicates he was a recognized member of the early Christian community.
namesAndTitles: The name Asynchritus appears only once in Scripture, in Romans 16:14, with no specific meaning or title given. It is a proper name without additional explanatory significance provided in the biblical text.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Asynchritus beyond the fact that Paul sends him greetings. No other relational details are noted.
scriptureSignificance: Asynchritus is significant primarily as a recipient of Paul's personal greetings in Romans 16:14, which reflects his inclusion among the faithful in the early church.
